LEARNING PATH · CLASS 48 · PLANTS & HOW THEY GROW · AGES 4–5

Plants & How They Grow — forty-one printable plant flashcards for kids.

Forty-one printable plant flashcards for ages four to five, all on this one page, in six shelves: the growing shelf, the plant parts shelf, the plant care shelf, the flowers and seeds shelf, the wild places shelf and the plant defense shelf. Every card shows a plant idea a child can hold in one hand TODAY — a seed to crack open, a celery race to run, a bud to watch burst, a root to count — with Download and Print buttons right under the picture. Pick a card, dig in, and the garden does the teaching.

Back to the Learning Path ↗
HOW THIS CLASS WORKS

One card. One look. One thing to try with your own hands.

Plants are the first science a child can grow — before the words germinate or chlorophyll, comes the feeling of a bean seed cracking open in a jam jar and a root diving down while a shoot climbs up. Every card in this class prints a plant idea with four labeled words: the growing cards walk the seed’s road stage by stage, the parts cards open the plant like a machine, the care cards hand over the gardener’s checklist, the flowers-and-seeds cards follow the bee’s errand, the wild-places cards travel from desert to pond to rainforest, and the defense cards show how plants fight back. You do not need a garden — you need one jar, one bean and a sunny window.

The shelves follow a young gardener’s year. The Growing Shelf starts with the crack-pop-sprout moment every kid remembers forever. The Plant Parts Shelf looks closer — root jobs, stem jobs, the leaf’s green magic, the seed’s packed lunch. The Plant Care Shelf sorts soil, follows the water and waits out the winter. The Flowers & Seeds Shelf runs the bee’s errand from blossom to brand-new seed. The Wild Places Shelf crosses the desert, the pond and the rainforest. And the Plant Defense Shelf meets the survivors — thorns, armor, camouflage and the helper crew who keep the whole garden standing. Do one card a day, and by summer the windowsill is a jungle.

AROUND THE SCHOOL

Where the plant lessons grow up.

Science, Nature & Discovery in Class 31 · Ages 4–5 ↗Animals & Their Habitats in Class 36 · Ages 4–5 ↗Fruits & Vegetables in Class 22 · Ages 3–5 ↗The Learning Path ↗

Class 31 runs the experiments — seeds sprouting, sink or float, the water cycle — and this class names the plant science those experiments ride on. Class 36 walks the animal habitats, and the Wild Places Shelf here is the plants’ half of the same map: the desert, the pond, the forest. Class 22 names the fruits and vegetables, and this class shows WHY the fruit exists — every apple is a seed’s bodyguard. And when you want the next class, the Learning Path holds all forty-nine in order — and the whole deck prints again from the Plants & How They Grow parents’ shelf.

Plant a card, grow a gardener. Every card here hands you one thing the windowsill can prove by bedtime — a seed cracked open, a root counted, a bud watched into flower. That is the whole lesson, and it is already yours.
